sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Culinary and Ceremonial Grade Matcha

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil law system with hybrid private-law institutions; private interest foundations codified under Law 25 of 1995
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (entered into force 2012)
EU-Central America Association Agreement covering Panama (provisionally applied from 2013)
Panama-Netherlands Agreement on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2003)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework) as amended by Law 70 of 2019; Executive Decree No. 153 of 2016; Law 129 of 22 December 2020; Executive Decree No. 170 of 23 December 2020 establishing the central beneficial ownership registry for legal entities; Private Interest Foundations governed by Law 25 of 12 June 1995 as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry and Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama; alternatively Consular Legalization at a Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of founder's passport or other government-issued identification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or civil registry of the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing legitimate source of endowment funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin bank of the founder or depositing bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention or Consular Legalization according to the origin country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the resident agent and foundation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in origin country and Notary Public of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the origin country's designated authority; if required, Consular Legalization by Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate existence of any foreign commercial counterparty named in the pre-incorporation procurement contracts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or company register of the counterparty's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all foundation council members, founder, beneficiaries, protectors, resident agent and material counterparties against the Panamanian PEP database, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, INTERPOL and domestic anti-corruption prosecutor lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person, including source of wealth and source of funds documentation, senior management approval and continuous transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General del Registro Público, Online Name Search and Reservation Module (e-Título portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be expressed in Spanish or in Roman/Latin script transliteration. Panamanian law requires that the chosen name be distinguishable, not contrary to public order or good customs, and not identical or confusingly similar to existing companies or foundations. A foreign trade mark may be used as a complementary denomination only after the statutory foundation name is cleared and registered.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal (recurso de reconsideración o apelación) to the Director General of the Registro Público within the time limit stated in the rejection notice, generally ten calendar days from notification under Ley 38 de 2000. The appeal must explain that the requested name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, that it contains no prohibited token absent required ministerial approval, and that it complies with naming public order. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may file a judicial action before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice of Panama. The applicant may also withdraw the rejected name and file a fresh reservation within the remaining validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office facilities are permitted for a low-risk private interest foundation engaged in cross-border procurement and distribution of organic matcha powder, provided the licensed resident agent maintains a physical registered office in Panama and full client due diligence files. The foundation may use the resident agent's address for statutory correspondence. For banking and counterparty risk purposes, some banks may require a physical operating address in addition to the registered agent address; a pure offshore virtual office is generally acceptable for this industry classification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 5% annualized likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection or registry verification for a low-risk PIF. The likelihood rises to 10-15% if the foundation engages in high-volume cross-border wire transfers through multiple Panamanian or foreign banks, or if the transaction value exceeds customary low-risk thresholds.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de julio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations, as amended) and Executive Decree No. 20 of 26 June 1996; relevant articles 1-7, 19-21, and 39-40.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section, Private Interest Foundation Registry (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura Constitutiva / Acta de Fundación) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and subsequently inscribed in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The Foundation Charter must specify an initial endowment of identifiable assets; no escrow account is required. A nominal cash endowment of USD 100 is common, and assets in kind may satisfy the requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: The Foundation Council accepts the endowment subscribed by the Founder as itemized in the Foundation Charter, and such assets constitute the foundation's initial patrimony. RESOLVED SECOND: The registered office designated in the Charter is adopted, and the Resident Agent's acceptance is approved. RESOLVED THIRD: The Council members named in the Charter are appointed as officeholders, with the Chairman and Secretary-Treasurer designated to administer assets, open bank accounts, execute matcha trade documentation, and engage professional advisers. RESOLVED FOURTH: All acts antecedent to this resolution, including regulatory filings and the DGI taxpayer application, are ratified and continued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Search and Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a public-registry name search for the proposed entity name, including the suffix Fundación or Foundation. If available, reserve the name for 30 calendar days through the online portal or in-person form to prevent conflicting registration.
required_dossiers: Application letter with proposed foundation name
Identity document of the proposed founder representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusingly similar or prohibited, submit up to three alternative names. Administrative reconsideration may be filed within the registry's appeal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Foundation Charter before Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder, or an attorney-in-fact, executes before a Panamanian notary the Foundation Charter in Spanish or in a certified bilingual text. The Charter must state the foundation's name, purpose (cross-border procurement and distribution of organic matcha powder), registered office, initial endowment, Foundation Council composition, registered agent, and beneficiary rules. The notary records the original in his or her protocol.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter
Valid passport or identity card of Founder and Foundation Council members
Foundation name reservation certificate
Registered Agent acceptance letter
Statement of initial endowment assets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any notarial observation is cured by amending the draft and re-executing the charter before the same notary. Supplementary protocol pages may be signed if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section, Private Interest Foundation Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first notarial copy of the executed Foundation Charter with a cover letter and official filing receipt. The Registry reviews legal formalities, assigns a folio, and certifies the legal existence of the foundation. A certified copy of the inscribed charter should be obtained after approval.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the Foundation Charter
Notary protocol certificate
Filing fee payment receipt
Registered Agent appointment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a reparo or objection, submit corrected provisions and supporting exhibits within the granted cure period. If final refusal is given, file a recurso de apelación before the Director General of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Identification and Municipal Operations Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and the Municipal Treasury of the Alcaldía de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the foundation's tax identification number (NIT/RUC) using the certified registry excerpt. Thereafter, if the foundation maintains a physical premises in Panama, file the Aviso de Operación and obtain the Municipal Business License. For a purely extraterritorial trading structure, coordinate with DGI to confirm the non-resident filing posture.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Registered Agent certificate of good standing
Proof of registered office address
Original identity documents of Foundation Council members
Foundation bank reference or opening commitment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Mismatches in the entity name, address, or Council data are cured by filing a rectification form before the DGI and the Municipality. Municipal fee assessments may be contested by a written reconsideration petition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organize First Foundation Council Meeting and Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian bank regulated by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the formal meeting of the Foundation Council, adopt the first board resolution, and record the minutes in the foundation's books. Open a bank account in the name of the foundation, deposit the initial endowment, and obtain a bank reference letter evidencing the funded patrimony.
required_dossiers: Certified Foundation Charter and registry folio
NIT/RUC certificate
Foundation Council first meeting minutes
Beneficial ownership declaration
Bank account application and client due diligence forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, provide a notarized statement of source of funds and prior-period records. Alternatively, choose a bank with established Panamanian private interest foundation practice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Product Sanitary Registration and Physical/Occupational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Food Safety Department; Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before importation or local distribution of organic matcha powder, submit the product label, technical file, organic certification, and certificate of free sale to MINSA for a food sanitary registration. If the foundation operates a warehouse in Panama, obtain fire-safety clearance and the environmental notification. Pure trading/warehousing does not trigger an industrial manufacturing permit.
required_dossiers: MINSA sanitary registration application
Product label and full specification sheet
Certificate of Free Sale from the country of origin
Organic matcha certificate issued by an accredited organic certifier
Warehouse lease or ownership proof
Bomberos fire-safety inspection application
MiAMBIENTE Category I environmental notification form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where MINSA queries the dossier, file additional laboratory analyses and corrected labels. A denial of registration may be appealed through the Ministry's administrative reconsideration process within 30 calendar days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias; applicable only if local blending, grinding, or repacking of matcha powder is later introduced.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Aviso de Operación/Business License; MINSA Food Sanitary Registration for imported matcha powder; optional organic certification import acceptance

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Notification for a trading and distribution warehouse with no processing; full EIA not required for packaged matcha powder storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge is generated by sealed-pack trading; sanitary effluents must comply with municipal sewer standards and Executive Decree No. 65 of 2019. Airborne dust/VOC emissions are not expected; any future blending or grinding line will require baghouse filtration and compliance with MiAMBIENTE air-quality thresholds applicable to food-processing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety certificate; municipal structural occupancy permit; and occupational health clearance from MITRADEL and MINSA for storage or handling staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (General Directorate of Revenue, 'DGI') of the Panamanian Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas); online fiscal portal: e-Tributa (https://e-tributa.dgi.gob.pa), with the DGI public site at https://www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must obtain the unified Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC, historically also referred to as NIT) before issuing ITBMS-invoiced transactions or claiming export zero-rating. Standard operating procedure: (1) prepare a certified Spanish-language copy of the PIF's registered charter (Acta Fundacional) recorded with the Panamanian Public Registry; (2) designate a resident agent or legal representative and provide their identity document; (3) submit the unified registration form (Formulario Único de Registro) and supporting identification documents either online through e-Tributa or at a DGI service window; (4) obtain the RUC certificate and digital access credentials; (5) activate the foundation's electronic fiscal mailbox for the mandatory electronic invoicing system and annual tax filings. Temporary single-transaction RUC registration is available to non-resident sellers, but the territorial zero-rating protocol normally requires full RUC status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not adopt a US-style check-the-box election or OECD hybrid-mismatch rules. A PIF is, by default, a separate legal and taxable person (not a pass-through trust) whose assessable income is limited to Panama-source income under the territorial tax model. Statutory elections relevant to effective taxation: (i) the simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen Especial de Pequeños Contribuyentes) for gross annual turnover up to B/.36,000, which reduces accounting and filing obligations; (ii) the election to use DGI-accredited electronic accounting records; and (iii) the freedom to select an accounting currency and taxable-year period, with the calendar year as default. Panama is an OECD member and participant in the BEPS Inclusive Framework, but its domestic law does not provide hybrid-mismatch election mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — a value-added tax (VAT) levied on the transfer of movable goods, service supplies, and imports in Panama, complemented by municipal sales/use-type taxation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0 (Balboa, 1:1 with USD) — registration in the RUC is compulsory whenever a person or entity habitually carries out economic activities in Panama; a reduced-compliance simplified taxpayer regime is available where rolling 12-month gross taxable turnover does not exceed B/.36,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic fiscal invoicing applies to ITBMS-registered traders through the DGI's Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SIE). Approved invoicing software or ERP providers transmit invoices in the DGI-defined XML schema to the e-Tributa platform, where the DGI validates the fiscal sequence, affixes a digital acceptance code, and communicates status in real time before the invoice is legally issued. B2B and B2C electronic invoices must contain the DGI digital stamp and QR code; printed invoices require a DGI-authorized cryptographic imprint. Invoices not cleared by the DGI cannot support input-credit claims, and repeated clearance failures trigger automated compliance blocks against the RUC.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The Panamanian Código Fiscal zero-rates exports of goods at 0% ITBMS when the sale involves physical departure of merchandise from Panama to a non-Panamanian destination under a completed customs export declaration, with title and risk transferred to the foreign buyer. For the organic matcha powder distribution scope, zero-rating requires: (a) the supplier/foundation to be RUC-registered; (b) goods confined to the national customs territory and then definitively exported, or transshipped under customs control; (c) invoices naming the overseas purchaser and denominated in a freely convertible currency; (d) payment demonstrably entering Panama from abroad; and (e) underlying purchase, inventory, and tonnage-reconciliation records substantiating the exported quantity. Transactions executed wholly offshore where goods never enter Panamanian territory are outside the territorial scope and are therefore not taxable rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / DUA) endorsed by the Panamanian Customs Authority (Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill consigned to the overseas buyer evidencing physical departure from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT credit note evidencing settlement from the foreign buyer within 180 days of export
Zero-rated commercial invoice and purchase order identifying goods, quantities, unit prices, and HS 0902.10 classification for organic matcha powder
Supplier invoices and warehouse or import records reconciling the exported tonnage to substantiate any input ITBMS credit offset by zero-rated sales
Foundation board or governing-body resolution authorizing the specific cross-border transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit any zero-rated sales and associated input-credit refund claims within the statutory limitation period. A disallowed export claim triggers: (i) retroactive nullification of the 0% rate, reassessment of 7% ITBMS on the full invoice value, and reversal of input credits; (ii) monthly statutory default interest from the original due date; (iii) administrative surcharges and progressive fines under the Código Fiscal, generally from 50% to 100% of the corrected tax for negligent underpayment and up to treble the tax for fraudulent documentation; and (iv) criminal tax-fraud referral of the foundation's officers and resident agent, with custodial penalties. Consistent failure to substantiate exports can lead to RUC suspension, denial of future refund claims, and reclassification of foreign receipts as Panama-source taxable revenue with the corresponding income tax exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No traditional central bank exists in Panama. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Panama Superintendency of Banks, SBP) is the financial regulator and de facto foreign-exchange conduct authority; the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) is the AML/CFT financial-intelligence unit; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the State's fiscal agent and clearing-house supervisor; the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) handles monetary integration policy. Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility across both current and capital account lines. The Balboa (PAB) exists solely as coinage at an immutably fixed 1:1 parity with the United States dollar; US banknotes are unlimited legal tender. There are no exchange-control licenses, import/export FX restrictions, profit-remittance permits, or capital-transaction approvals. Non-resident beneficiaries of a Panamanian PIF may receive distributions freely without Panamanian exchange-control clearance or withholding tax. The only operative hurdles are documentary: banks must verify lawful origin of funds and genuine commercial purpose. Direct trading activity should be carried through a Panamanian stock corporation (S.A.) owned by the PIF to respect the foundation's asset-management scope under Law 25 of 1995 and avoid the appearance of the PIF itself conducting a merchandising business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export-proceeds surrender rules do not exist in Panama. There is no statutory timeline for USD or foreign-currency repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no requirement to sell export receipts through any designated bank, and no central-bank approval of trade settlements. Exporters and trade intermediaries may retain, borrow, or invest proceeds in any currency. Banking-AML rules nevertheless require that export receipts be traceable to genuine commercial transactions; banks apply internal scrutiny to large or fragmented wire credits under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Anti-Money-Laundering Resolution.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM. Panamanian law (Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Banking Rules) requires any operator receiving deposits or performing payment services for Panamanian client structures to be a licensed bank or an SBP-sanctioned fintech-sandbox institution. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Revolut Business are not licensed to hold PIF accounts in Panama and generally decline Panama-connected entity structures. Their utility is limited to ancillary, low-balance receipts in Japan or China supplier markets; they cannot serve as a PIF's primary treasury or settlement rail. The entrenched correspondent network of Banco General, Banistmo, and Multibank remains the legally robust alternative.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is the default mandate. Under SBP consolidated KYC standards, signatories and UBOs of legal-entity accounts must be identified through a personal interview; banks generally require at least the granting director or an appointed attorney-in-fact to appear at the Panama City branch, or at an overseas correspondent branch with apostilled authorization. Remote video onboarding is accepted only for low-risk structures and usually still demands a prior physical appointment for the PIF beneficiary or grantor. Foundation Council members who are not designated signatories are exempt from physical appearance. In practice, remote opening is possible via a notarized and apostilled power of attorney to the bank officer, executed under enhanced due diligence, but Tier-1 banks apply heightened scrutiny to PIFs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Grantor/beneficiary anonymity characteristic of a Private Interest Foundation - bank suspects an opaque asset-holding vehicle with untraceable individuals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Pacto Fundacional (foundation charter) including object clauses; formal letter of designation listing grantor, Foundation Council, protector, and all beneficiaries; certificate of inscription of the foundation in the Public Registry of Panama; beneficial-ownership declaration in line with Law 23 of 2015 and UBO register amendments; resolution confirming the absence of bearer shares and establishing the foundation's passive holding role.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated source of wealth or funds associated with cross-border procurement of organic matcha powder from Japan or China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-file dossier: executed master supply agreement with a registered tea mill or supplier; per-shipment purchase orders; commercial and pro-forma invoices; Certificates of Analysis and organic certifications (JAS, USDA, EU organic as applicable); transport documents including bills of lading and air-waybills; customs and phytosanitary clearances; bank statements demonstrating historical fund flows; tax registration and filing evidence of the underlying trading company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or beneficiary located in a sanctioned or FATF-listed jurisdiction, with indicators of trade mis-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening outputs for all parties and banks; AML/ABC policies; evidence that supply-chain jurisdictions such as Japan, PRC, United States, EU, and Panama are not under OFAC, UN, or EU asset-freeze; independent price benchmarking for matcha grades to rebut mis-invoicing; third-party due-diligence reports from providers such as Dow Jones or KYC; correspondent Nostro bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Scope mismatch: the PIF appears to conduct an active commercial business incompatible with its private-interest-foundation purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate group chart showing the PIF solely owns a Panamanian S.A. executing the ISIC 4631 wholesale trade; the S.A.'s Aviso de Operación and tax registration; PIF council resolutions authorizing capital contributions and intercompany financing; loan agreements or equity-credit notes conforming to arm's-length conditions; consolidated financial statements and tax filings evidencing that all trading income is booked to the S.A. and not the PIF.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Fully liberalized routing. Capital can be injected by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire from any jurisdiction without a Panama exchange-control permit. Recommended practice: use a clear beneficiary narrative such as 'Capital contribution to PA_PIF - matcha trade holding entity'; designate SWIFT Purpose Code 'CAPT' for equity capital, 'INVC' for intercompany loans, or 'AGRM' for trade prepayments; pre-notify the RMA and correspondent bank with a council resolution, UBO disclosure, and signed financing agreement; ensure the sender's bank KYC matches the foundation's entity names to avoid rejection. Panama banks verify the tie between the wire narrative and the trade contract, so the corporate holding structure and underlying S.A. purchase orders must accompany settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for nostro-to-nostro) telegraphic transfers for matcha procurement from Japan and China; banks may require supplier invoice, purchase order, and packing list for amounts above USD 50,000 or for disbursements to new counterparties. Irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit at sight are available through Banco General, Banistmo, and Multibank when supplier risk or high-value procurements demand bank-backed clearing. Domestic ACH clearing via Panama's Cámara de Compensación through Banco Nacional covers local operational expenses only. All rails settle in USD without external FX approval; documentation retention is essential to distinguish genuine trade disbursements from potential capital leakage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/JPY forward contracts (10-day to 12-month tenors) through Banco General or correspondent investment banks, aligned to matcha import payment dates from Japan
Offshore USD/CNH deliverable forwards, using the offshore yuan (CNH) rather than onshore CNY, permitted without SBP pre-approval
Cross-currency interest-rate or plain currency swaps in USD/JPY and USD/CNH where trade flows are multi-shipment and staggered across fiscal quarters
Vanilla FX options such as USD call/CNH put or USD call/JPY put purchasable from SBP-licensed banks for treasury hedging protection without speculative prohibited use
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY onshore or other limited-convertibility Asian currencies, permissible for hedge-accounting purposes notwithstanding the deliverable CNH alternative

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax (Pago del Impuesto Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; payment is made through authorized Panamanian banks and proof is kept by the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on July 15 of each calendar year; the first year's tax must be paid before registration with the Public Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a 10% surcharge and monthly statutory interest; non-payment for three consecutive years exposes the foundation to administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registro Público, subject to the foundation charter's winding-up provisions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review and confirmation of statutory registers and beneficial-ownership information (internal record maintained by the Foundation Council)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent; available to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), DGI, and the Public Registry on lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of foundation registration, and within 30 days after any change in the Foundation Council or beneficiaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate government filing penalty; inaccurate or incomplete registers are assessed under Law 23 of 2015 and Law 70 of 2019, with monetary fines, and may render notarial or banking acts unenforceable until corrected

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Law 25 of 1995 for a Private Interest Foundation; an independent audit is required only if the foundation charter, Foundation Council, or protector mandates it. No turnover or asset threshold is imposed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory statutory accounting framework is prescribed; finances may be recorded under IFRS as adopted in Panama or another consistent accounting basis. If Panamanian-source income arises, supporting books must substantiate the territorial tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Private Interest Foundation has no shares; shareholding-transfer confirmation procedures are not applicable. Beneficiary rights are transferred through the foundation charter and reflected by an update to the beneficiary register. No annual UBO filing is made to the Public Registry. Under Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 2019, the registered agent must hold current beneficial-ownership records and update them within 30 days of any change in Foundation Council members or beneficiaries. A zero-change filing is not statutorily required; an anniversary confirmation is recommended for record integrity.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members, Register of Beneficiaries, Minutes Book of the Foundation Council

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,200 per year, covering the Panamanian registered agent, registered office address, and handling of government filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not mandatory for a Private Interest Foundation under Law 25; if required by the charter, a full audit typically ranges from USD 4,000–8,000; a voluntary compilation or review ranges from USD 1,500–3,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No preferential statutory rate for matcha powder distribution; the territorial regime applies, excluding foreign-source income. Potential lesser rates only under specific regimes (e.g., SEM/REIC headquarters incentives) not routinely applicable to a wholesale distribution PIF.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 150 (Informe de Rentas) filed by corporate taxpayers through Panama's Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) electronic portal, e-Tax 2.0.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the last day of the third month following the fiscal year end; for calendar-year taxpayers, filing and payment due by 31 March.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Panama-source gross revenue generated from wholesale matcha powder sales and export procurement commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income derived from activities physically performed or assets located in Panama; exclude income from sales executed abroad by foreign affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and directly allocable commercial expenses, including shipping, storage, USDA/ceremonial grade certification testing, and brokers' fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses only to the extent they are documented and connected to Panama-source income; transfer pricing documentation required for related-party costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after expense deductions and prior-year loss carryforwards (up to 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF is purely a holding entity with foreign bank deposit interest and foreign dividend income, Box 7 should show zero Panama-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments already paid monthly (Anticipos), including the 2% gross-revenue-based advance or the 10% net-income-based provision.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owner should ensure advance payments are made under the PIF's RUC; otherwise the DGI will charge compensatory interest and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: fine of 5% of the tax due, plus 2% monthly interest on unpaid amounts up to 24%. Formal non-compliance fines range from USD 10 to USD 5,000. Non-filing may trigger an estimated assessment with a 15% penalty, and publication of the entity in Panama's tax debtor registry.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid from profits already subject to corporate income tax; 20% on distributions from untaxed offshore profits (often relevant for PIFs).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a very limited DTA network. To claim treaty relief, the non-resident must provide a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, file the relevant DGI application, and require the paying Panamanian entity to obtain a reduced withholding authorization before distributions. If no treaty applies or documentation is incomplete, the statutory 10% dividend WHT is withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties for the use of IP or trademarks within Panama are subject to 12.5% withholding; interest on Panamanian-sourced debt is also subject to 12.5% withholding (exemption may apply for certain bank loans). Treaty rates, where applicable, typically range from 2.5%-10% for interest and 5%-12.5% for royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama (USD/Balboa): mandatory Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 350) required when annual gross income exceeds USD 10 million; contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation is triggered when related-party transactions exceed USD 3 million, or when the taxpayer qualifies under the TP regime.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), introduced by Law 248 of 2021 and related rules, require all relevant legal entities conducting 'relevant activities' (including distribution and service center operations) to maintain adequate physical offices, local employees, and core income-generating activities in Panama. A PIF that merely holds matcha contract rights and invoices from a mailbox address without local substance will be exposed to mandatory substance declarations, annual reporting obligations, and risk of administrative dissolution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Misrepresentation of Panama-Source Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately misclassifying Panama distribution sales as 'foreign' in order to remove matcha profits from the 25% territorial tax base, or using false invoices to inflate costs and reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for up to 5 years, fines of 2 to 10 times the evaded tax, plus retroactive tax assessments, monthly interest at 2%, and an additional 10% surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or foundation council members who sign false tax returns may have the corporate veil pierced; they are individually liable for civil restitution, may face criminal prosecution, travel bans, and disqualification from standing as company directors in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Complete Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF with zero employees, no physical office in Panama, no local board meetings, and using a registered agent only as a token, while claiming Panamanian holding advantages or treaty benefits for matcha royalty/interest streams.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Panama's ESR Law and Fiscal Code: fines from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000, cancellation of the Foundation's PIF registration, automatic denial of treaty or withholding relief, and re-characterization of income as Panama-source with 25% corporate tax plus penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation directors are jointly and severally liable for ESR fines if they fail to file economic substance declarations; they can be banned from entering public procurement contracts for up to 8 years and barred from directorship of any Panamanian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Non-Compliance in Trade Channel
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF as a pass-through instrument to conceal the true beneficiary of cross-border matcha trade payments, creating false commodity invoices to justify large wire transfers, or failing to register the beneficial owner with the UAF (Financial Analysis Unit).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's AML Code (Law 23 of 2015 and related FATF/CRS regulations): imprisonment for 2 to 4 years, corporate fines up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, asset forfeiture, and automatic listing in the national money-laundering offenders registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers involved in or wilfully ignoring suspicious matcha trade flows face minimum 3-year prison sentences, freezing orders, travel bans during investigation, and personal seizure of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File, Pay, or Withhold Tax; Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the Form 150 filing deadline, failing to submit Form 350 when opting for TP documentation thresholds are met, or failing to withhold the 10% dividend WHT on repatriations to the foreign beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax due; monthly interest of 2% on unpaid tax up to 24%; TP non-filing penalties of up to USD 10,000; DGI may levy estimated assessments plus a 15% enhancement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for withheld dividend taxes not remitted to the DGI; they may be subject to departure restrictions (travel bans) and administrative arrest until the debt is paid, plus civil enforcement against personal assets.
